title: Opal FinLabs outbound playbook - doodles
content:
Notes to self / quick sketch for Opal FinLabs outreach and pilot proposal

Background (quick)
- Opal FinLabs: mid-stage fintech focused on real-time risk scoring and liquidity insights for SMB lenders.
- Tech stack: Python services, Kafka streaming, AWS (us-west), in-house features for scoring. Heavy tail on low-latency inference during credit decision path (sub-150ms SLO per request).
- Concern: token-level cost and privacy (customer data), thinking about private deployment or dedicated GPUs.
- Known contact: Elena Ruiz (Head of ML Ops) and Tobias Grant (VP Product). Intro came via demo day — follow-up needed.

Primary pain hypotheses
- Latency spikes at peak underwriting load; queues cause request timeouts and lost conversions.
- Cost unpredictability with current cloud-hosted models — variability due to bursty traffic.
- Data residency / compliance: some customers require strict isolation, cannot send raw PII to third-party hosted models.

How Redwood helps (concise messaging)
- Predictable latency: Dedicated capacity + autoscale policies that keep p50/p95 under 120ms for their sequence lengths.
- Cost control: batching + prefix cache reduces token spend for repeated prompt patterns (template prompts in scoring flow).
- Private/VPC option: full control plane in their VPC or on-prem for compliance-heavy lenders.
- Rollout safety: canary routing and fallback to a smaller model if peak capacity hits, avoid 504s.

Top lines for an initial email (A/B candidates)
A) Subject: Cut underwriting time spikes by 40% — quick idea for Opal FinLabs\nHi Elena — saw Opal’s demo at FinTech West. We’ve worked with lending stacks to keep decisioning latency predictable at peak load (p95 < 120ms) while cutting token costs via smart prefix caching and batching. Would you be open to a 20-minute call to see a short pilot that runs in your VPC?
– Maya

B) Subject: private inference + cost guardrails for lender workflows
Tobias — short note: we help teams move model inference behind their VPC and add deterministic autoscale + fallback policies so your underwriting SLOs don’t degrade during traffic bursts. 15–20m to show a sketch?

Cold call / LinkedIn pitch bullets (30s)
- Quick intro: Redwood Inference — we run inference so teams can ship LLM features with enterprise SLAs.
- Problem statement: underwriting latency spikes = revenue leakage. We pin models, run in-VPC, and provide cost/latency guarantees.
- Micro ask: 15 minutes to map where your decision stack calls the model and show a small pilot design.

Objection handling (short)
- "We can host models ourselves" -> "Totally — some teams do. We offer a dedicated runtime and observability that usually saves 30–50% of ops time and reduces per-token cost via batching/kv caching; we can pair with your infra team for a short proof-of-concept (2–4 weeks)."
- "Data residency concerns" -> "We offer Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed keys and audit logs; customers keep full control over data."
- "Will it integrate with Kafka/Rest endpoints?" -> "Yes — we accept HTTP/gRPC and have connectors/examples for Kafka-triggered inference; Solutions Eng will help map it out."

Pilot idea (opportunity sketch)
- Objective: reduce p95 decision latency by 30% during peak and demonstrate 20% token/unit cost reduction.
- Scope: 2-week technical POC in their dev VPC, using a representative prompt set (we'll send prompt capture artifact).
- Metrics to measure: p50/p95 latency, median tokens per decision, successful decisions / conversion lift, cost per 1,000 decisions.
- Minimal infra: 1-2 dedicated GPU workers (g4dn/g5 equivalent) + routing policy to fallback endpoint.
- Success criteria: p95 < 150ms and cost per decision decreased by >15% vs their baseline.

Technical checklist for Solutions Eng (notes)
- Need prompt examples + typical sequence lengths (avg tokens in request + expected completion tokens).
- Confirm throughput: expected qps at peak and burst factor (x2/x5).
- Authentication: SSO and KMS requirement? Elena likely wants KMS/HSM.
- Telemetry: want token-level cost and latency breakdowns. Build a Grafana dashboard during POC.
- Data capture: ensure we have sanitized prompt set for regression tests and evals.

Pricing ask (draft language)
- Suggest a short-term pilot credit + usage-based trial: Redwood covers infra for POC; if they convert to Dedicated, propose 3-month committed tier with a pilot-to-prod credit applied.

Meeting prep checklist (to bring)
- One-pager: low-risk architecture for POC (VPC-private control plane).
- Demo recording: prior lending customer (anonymized) showing p95 improvement.
- Prompt capture template + short eval: 20 prompts that represent core decision flow.
- A rough TCO comparison sheet (their current cloud inference vs Redwood dedicated).

Open questions / TODOs
- Ask Elena for a representative full request payload (anonymized).
- Confirm compliance/regulator constraints that would force on-prem rather than VPC.
- Check if they use KMS provider (AWS KMS vs HashiCorp) — list in onboarding.
- Julian to draft POC network diagram (due: 2025-02-20).

Next steps (internal)
- Cold email + LinkedIn sequence (Julian to send first pass by 2025-02-14).
- Prep POC one-pager + pricing sketch (Priya owns).
- Sync with Solutions Eng to confirm feasibility (quick triage call).

Random scribbles / fallback lines
- "If we can't do full private, propose a hybrid: tokenization and caching local, generation in dedicated hosted region with strict routing."
- "Pitch the audit trail: every inference call has a traceable audit record for compliance teams."
- Short anecdote: another lender reduced decision latency by 37% after switching to pin + dedupe caching — good quick-use case for story.

Signed-off: Maya (quick working notes — rough, keep for next sync)
